title: Sara Lee Dutch Apple Pie
subtitle: Bakes from frozen, with a streusel topping you add before it goes in.

items: 1 Sara Lee Dutch Apple Pie (34 oz.), frozen, with its streusel packet
Baking sheet (lined with aluminum foil for easier cleanup)
Aluminum foil, to shield the crust edges if needed

steps.title: Preheat with a baking sheet
paragraphs: Preheat oven to 400°F with a baking sheet on the center rack. Keep the pie frozen until you're ready to bake.

steps.title: Add the streusel
paragraphs: Remove the frozen pie from the carton and take off the plastic overwrap. Open the streusel packet, break up the topping with a fork, and spread it evenly over the pie.

steps.title: Bake
paragraphs: Place the frozen pie on the preheated baking sheet on the center rack. Bake at 400°F for 60 to 65 minutes, until the topping is an even golden brown.
Check at 45 minutes. If the crust edges are browning too fast, cover them with foil, but leave the center uncovered.

steps.title: Check the temperature
paragraphs: Confirm the inside of the pie reaches 165°F with a baking thermometer.

steps.title: Cool
paragraphs: Remove the pie from the oven while it's still on the baking sheet. Never handle the pie pan by its edges; the filling is hot. Cool at room temperature before cutting: about 45 minutes for a warm pie, or 2 hours for a cooler one.

blocks.content: Keep the pie frozen until you're ready to bake. It needs about an hour in a 400°F oven, which is a different temperature from everything else, so it's easiest to bake before the turkey goes in or while it roasts if you have a second oven.
After baking, cover leftovers with foil. They keep up to 2 days at room temperature or up to 4 days refrigerated.
